messages.subject: NIMBLE June workshop will now be a virtual workshop, June 3-5
messages.subject_clean: NIMBLE June workshop will now be a virtual workshop, June 3-5
messages.body_plain:
All,

For obvious reasons, we are changing our planned in-person NIMBLE workshop to be a virtual workshop held completely online. To accommodate participants on the East Coast, we are switching to a three day format, June 3-5 from 9 am - 2 pm PDT (noon - 5 pm EDT).

Full details can be found here: https://r-nimble.org/registration-open-for-online-nimble-short-course-june-3-5-2020.

For those of you who hadn't registered for the in-person workshop, we invite you to participate. You can register here: https://na.eventscloud.com/540175. Registration is $120 (regular) or $60 (grad student).

For those of you already registered for the in-person format, I'll be sending a separate email with instructions on how to either switch to the online workshop or cancel with a full refund.

Chris, for the NIMBLE team

messages.subject: nimbleEcology: custom NIMBLE distributions for ecologists
messages.subject_clean: nimbleEcology: custom NIMBLE distributions for ecologists
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'd like to advertise an auxiliary NIMBLE package, nimbleEcology.

nimbleEcology contains a set of distributions corresponding to some common ecological models. These distributions are implemented to integrate over latent states in the model. It's designed to integrate smoothly with NIMBLE model coding.

The following distributions are available:
dOcc  (occupancy model)
dDynOcc  (dynamic occupancy model)
dHMM  (hidden Markov model)
dDHMM  (dynamic hidden Markov model)
dCJS  (Cormack-Jolly-Seber or mark-recapture model)
dNmixture  (N-mixture model)
nimbleEcology and its documentation are now available on CRAN <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nimbleEcology/index.html> and GitHub <https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimbleEcology>. It was also discussed in the recent Ecol & Evol paper "One size does not fit all: Customizing MCMC methods for hierarchical models using NIMBLE" (Ponisio et al., 2020 <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.6053>). See also this blog post <https://r-nimble.org/nimbleecology-custom-nimble-distributions-for-ecologists> with example code on r-nimble.org <http://r-nimble.org>.

Thanks,
Ben Goldstein
